declarations.name: discrete_crossing_duality
declarations.doc: Discrete Steinhaus/Hex crossing duality (general marking).** On the board `Fin (m+1) × Fin (n+1)`, for an arbitrary decidable marking: either the marked cells contain a king-connected chain from the bottom row to the top row, or the free cells contain a rook-connected chain from the left column to the right column. Mechanism: pad the board with sentinels (marked bottom/top rows, free left/right columns), walk the marked/free interface with the right-hand rule from the pinned start dart, terminate by pigeonhole against predecessor uniqueness, and read the crossing off the exit; the king/rook asymmetry enters at the diagonal turn, which keeps the marked shore king-connected.

Thus the complete derived constraint topology is invariant under arbitrary finite residue orientation surgery and cannot select the positive chamber.

This is the level-vanishing step: an exponentially small bound on a fixed level polynomial along an unbounded set of integers forces the level to vanish identically.

exploration.name: tendsto_twoModeSource_div_deficit
exploration.doc: The central correction is of deficit order.** With the fixed-mode prolate asymptotics as hypotheses — both deficits vanish, the two total integrals converge to their limits, and the eigenvalue gap is asymptotically half the second deficit — the two-mode central value divided by the deficit converges to `-2^{-3/4} sqrt(3/11)`. Hence the radical depends on the support stratum of the metric, not on the values of its positive weights.

The residual between the two orders of crossing the `e`- and `f`-faces, `f ⊗ ex - e ⊗ fx`, is the explicit sum of degree-two Hochschild boundaries on the left. In the prime-dilation application, `e = P_m`, `f = P_n`, and `x = Q`. Thus the finite two-prime ordering defect vanishes in Hochschild homology.

No functional equation is used — only the Euler–Maclaurin identity at depth `N`.

declarations.doc: The Euler–Maclaurin function is the Hurwitz zeta function.** On `Re s > 1` it equals the convergent spectral series `∑_{n ≥ 0} (n+a)^{-s}`.

declarations.name: zeta_eq_emCarrier_sub

declarations.name: norm_riemannZeta_line_le_dyadic_em

declarations.name: norm_zeta_sub_gN_le

declarations.name: norm_riemannZeta_le_inv_abs_im

declarations.name: norm_riemannZeta_le_routeT_canonical

declarations.name: norm_riemannZeta_le_linear_of_re_ge_half

declarations.name: detPolyC_add_one_eq_of_zeta_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Zero detection.** At a zero of `ζ` in the right half plane the detection polynomial differs from `−1` by exactly the mollified Euler–Maclaurin remainder: `detPolyC N y ρ + 1 = M_y(ρ)·(−N^(1−ρ)/(ρ−1) + ρ·emTail N ρ)`.
